title: Slab starvation causing intermittent GPU OOMs and KV pointer snapshot drift across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Summary: Multiple customers (hosted, dedicated, private) reported sudden spikes of GPU OOMs and long-tail latency regressions during mixed short/long prompt workloads. Investigation indicates a slab allocation starvation pattern combined with stale KV pointer snapshots that prevents timely compaction. The allocator fails to reclaim small fragmented slabs under high session churn; stale snapshot references keep pages pinned leading to transient but severe memory pressure and kernel OOM cascades. This ticket tracks the patch, rollout and customer comms.
repro_steps: 1) Deploy runtime-1.20 with KV snapshotting enabled and prefix caching on a 16GB GPU node
2) Simulate high session churn: 200 concurrent short-chat sessions + periodic long-generation bursts (seq_len > 2k) for 10 minutes
3) Observe slab free lists shrinking; KV snapshot refcount for some pages remains >0 after session eviction
4) Trigger continuous batching path causing allocator attempts to satisfy a large request which results in GPU OOM and eviction retries
impact_summary: Intermittent OOMs across environments leading to failed requests, increased tail latency, canary alarms in Dedicated customers, and two P1 escalations from Hosted customers. Affected customers experienced request failures and degraded QoS for 2-7 minute windows before mitigations engaged.
mitigation: 1) Emergency config change: lower default max_batch_size for affected fleets to reduce peak transient working set (applied to Hosted region-us-west2)
2) Force early KV snapshot reap: background sweep job run across nodes (mitigates pinned pages for ~80% of incidents)
3) Temporary autoscale rule: spin additional dedicated nodes to spread active sessions and reduce slab contention for impacted customers
proposed_fix: 1) Introduce snapshot reference epoching: avoid indefinite pinning by associating snapshots with short-lived epoch tokens and expire stale epochs during compaction
2) Enhance slab allocator with proactive coalescing: detect micro-fragmentation pattern and merge adjacent free slabs older than threshold N seconds
3) Add low-overhead backpressure path for large-generation requests when free slab pool falls below soft threshold
4) Add unit+integration tests that simulate mixed churn and long-sequence bursts against the allocator and KV snapshot code paths
5) Code owner PR with runtime-1.22.1 target and canary flag to gate behavior behind config toggle
acceptance_criteria: No reproducible OOMs under the repro_steps with >1h run in staging with 95th latency within baseline
Automated regression tests added to CI that simulate churn + long sequences and assert no pinned pages > 30s
Canary rollout on 5% of Hosted traffic for 24h with zero P0 regressions and stable memory headroom
Customer-facing support notes and postmortem draft ready for affected customers
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR to runtime-1.22.1 branch behind feature flag
2) Deploy to internal staging with instrumented metrics and run 2h soak using load harness
3) Canary to Hosted region-us-west2 at 5% traffic for 24h; monitor memory/free-slab metrics and KV pinned-pages gauge
4) If green, increase to 30% and run 48h soak, then full-hosted rollout
5) For Dedicated customers: provide patch bundle and coordinate maintenance window; for Private customers provide patch + configuration guidance and a one-line migration script
qa_plan: Integration test: 3 variants of session churn + long gen using the infra load harness
Fuzz test: random allocation/free patterns for 30 minutes to validate coalescing correctness
Stress test: long-running 24h soak on a 16GB GPU node with periodic 2k+ token bursts
Security regression review: confirm no new unsafes in allocator path and run oss-fuzz where applicable
monitoring_and_alerting: Create alert: runtime.kv_pinned_pages_ratio > 0.08 for 2m -> notify runtime-oncall
Dashboard: runtime/memory/allocator (free slabs, frag ratio, pinned pages) linked to internal grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/runtime-allocator
Add synthetic canary: periodic generation that verifies free-slab headroom and KV snapshot GC within expected window
postmortem_notes: Root cause: interaction between epochless KV snapshot references and a slab allocator optimized for steady-state leading to pinned micro-pages during churn
Contributing factors: sudden mixture of short sessions + infrequent long generations; default batching heuristics creating transient spikes
Action items: implement fixes in this ticket, audit other snapshot paths, update runbooks for faster mitigation steps
customer_communications: Initial acknowledgement sent to affected customers on 2026-03-10 with mitigation steps and ETA
Follow-up: targeted Dedicated customer maintenance windows proposed for 2026-03-18
Post-deployment: share postmortem and improvements, offer dedicated support window
